content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 (no action): the 14:00–16:00 window is predicted at 97.9% service level, well above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The payments spike this morning traces to the UPI switch incident (INC-20261026-6474): upi_payment_failed calls ran at 385 against 88.8 expected and drove service level as low as 0.5%. For the disruption window of 14:00–16:00, however, doing nothing is predicted to give 97.9% overall, with 98.1% on payments and 97.6% on general. The abandon rate is predicted at 1.0% and the rest of the day at 95.9%. No policy is breached. Every alternative also clears the target, so none of them buys anything that matters.","trade_offs":["P1 (break delays, 2 agents moved from general, IVR callback) costs nothing but predicts slightly lower results: 97.5% overall and 96.9% on general. It disrupts breaks and draws on the general queue for no gain.","P2 (outage IVR message plus chat deflection) predicts the best window figures: 98.4% overall and 0.6% abandon. It costs INR 300 and breaches CX-01, because its message also covers payment_status_enquiry and not only upi_payment_failed.","P3 lifts payments to 98.8% and cuts abandon to 0.8%. It also breaches CX-01, lowers general to 96.3%, and adds overtime requests and an agent move.","Under P0, callers with failed UPI payments get no proactive outage message. That is a customer-experience gap, but the service-level target is still met."],"watch":"The IT ticket is still open and calls rose before it was detected. If upi_payment_failed volumes rise again or payments service level drops toward 80% during 14:00–16:00, revisit P1. A CX-01-compliant outage message limited to upi_payment_failed would be the next step."}
